propositions: The query ticket digest is re-sent in full on every judge call (12/12 times measured) despite being identical across a batch, consuming tokens in the volatile user block where caching cannot apply.
Moving the shared query digest from the user message into the system prompt makes it part of the cacheable prefix, enabling one cache write plus N-1 cheap reads per review batch.

The real cache floor for anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 is 1024 tokens (measured), not the 4096 documented for Opus; the hoisted prefix (846 tokens) falls short and produces no cache hits on the measured corpus.
Precision is preserved across the hoist: all 12 ordered-pair verdicts (relation, shared_artifact, confidence) remain identical between inline-digest and hoisted variants.

The token outcome is a measured regression of +936 input tokens (+5.8%) because the added orientation paragraph cost outweighs zero cache benefit, and this regression must be reported rather than absorbed.
Parallelizing the sequential judge loop requires warming the cache with one completed call before fanning out, to avoid N premium cache writes instead of 1 write plus N-1 reads.
